items.title: Live: Suspect due to face court over Trump press dinner incident as security preparations investigated
items.description: US Acting Attorney-General Todd Blanche says the shooter apprehended at the White House correspondents' dinner was likely targeting Donald Trump. Follow live.

items.title: Teacher of the month turned would-be assassin. Who is Cole Allen?
items.description: Details from the life of US President Donald Trump's would-be assassin paint a picture of a high achiever who took an abrupt turn towards political violence.

items.title: 'Superhero' politician shielded Kerry Kennedy at correspondents' dinner
items.description: Human rights activist Kerry Kennedy praises a "superhero" member of Congress for shielding her when an active shooter attempted to storm the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner.

items.title: Criminal history of man police are searching for over missing 5yo girl revealed
items.description: A man being sought in connection with the alleged abduction of five-year-old Sharon Granites near Alice Springs has a long history of violence and prison time in the Northern Territory.

items.title: RSL to review Welcome to Country policies after Anzac Day booing
items.description: RSL Australia will review its Welcome to Country guidelines after Indigenous elders were booed during Anzac Day services across the country.

items.title: Sabastian Sawe ran the marathon in an 'unbelievable time'. Here's why we can believe in it
items.description: Sabastian Sawe has smashed through one of athletics' unbreakable barriers by running a marathon faster than two hours. Some call it unbelievable, but the Kenyan runner has done everything he can to ensure it stands the test of time.

items.title: Betting on state secrets: The markets accused of cashing in on war
items.description: A US soldier accused of using classified information to place bets on a covert military operation has thrown a spotlight on the fast-growing world of prediction markets.

items.title: Mick Malthouse fought off alleged intruders with exercise bar, court told
items.description: Legendary AFL coach Mick Malthouse "swung an exercise pole" and hit an intruder in the head as he defended his family during an alleged attempted home invasion last year, a Melbourne court has heard.

items.title: Friday could be Tasmania's hottest May day in nearly 140 years
items.description: Tasmania is well into autumn, but firefighters remain on alert as late-season bushfires have threatened communities. This Friday marks the first day of May, and with it could come one of the state's hottest May days in nearly 140 years of record-keeping.

items.title: Maccas wins battle to set up in 'world's coolest street'
items.description: The fast food giant has been cleared to set up an outlet in the Melbourne suburb of Northcote after successfully challenging a council decision to block its restaurant plans.

items.title: Two dead in house fire on day family were due to move interstate
items.description: Two bodies found in a house that was extensively damaged by fire in the foothills of the NSW Blue Mountains are believed to be those of two missing children.

items.title: Citizen's arrest halts alleged tiny home thief in Queensland
items.description: A chance sighting of a social media post detailing the theft of two tiny homes leads to two friends making a dramatic citizen's arrest on the Sunshine Coast.

items.title: AFL boss says umpiring 'as good as it's been' despite admitting ARC errors
items.description: AFL football boss Greg Swann says most of the feedback he receives from the clubs surrounding the officiating in the league is positive despite a pair of controversial review calls in Round 7.

items.title: Four easy egg recipes to add to your regular rotation
items.description: If you're looking to add the humble egg into your weekly meals, we have you covered.

items.title: 'I know it's illegal': Artist behind 'Aussie' posters reveals new target
items.description: Peter Drew has been hanging his controversial posters around Australia for 10 years, and has no plans to stop.

items.title: 'She's like Will Ferrell': Why Kitty Flanagan said yes to Anne Edmonds
items.description: Everything Anne Edmonds has done over the last two decades has been leading to Bad Company, an unfettered satire of the theatre world the comedian created, wrote and stars in alongside Kitty Flanagan.

items.title: Paralympic champion shares emotional volatility after traumatic brain injury
items.description: Alexa Leary sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI) after a cycling accident at age 19. The two-time Paralympic gold medallist turned author is calling for a day to recognise TBI and the unique challenges it brings.

items.title: Climber sustains life-threatening injuries in fall near Mount Arapiles
items.description: A rock climber is recovering in hospital after falling from a rock face near Mount Arapiles in Victoria's west.

items.title: Two young girls die as WA records another dire weekend on roads
items.description: Two young girls, aged three and four, die more than a week after a car crash in Viveash, with the news emerging after another two fatalities on WA roads over the Anzac Day long weekend.

items.title: E-scooter rental companies say proposed laws threaten Qld viability
items.description: The government's proposed legislation — including new licensing requirements, a 10km/h speed limit on footpaths, and an age restriction — are expected to become law in July.

items.title: 'We live up here to escape': Residents unhappy with sand dredging proposal
items.description: A Dutch dredging company acknowledges concerns from some community members in northern Western Australia that public meetings should have been held earlier.

items.title: Pogačar looks unbeatable, but Seixas could be France's next new hope
items.description: Tadej Pogačar claims a third monument win out of four for the year at Liège-Bastogne-Liège, but a new power is rising in the form of 19-year-old Paul Seixas, with an unlikely Tour de France tilt seemingly on the cards.

items.title: PNG PM says Luai's visit 'sends a message' ahead of Chiefs' NRL entry
items.description: The Wests Tigers playmaker is the Chiefs' top target ahead of their NRL entry in 2028, and the Papua New Guinea prime minister says his trip to PNG shows the interest is mutual.

items.title: 'Security was extraordinarily lax': ABC's Americas editor on how the shooting played out
items.description: ABC's Americas editor John Lyons said there was less security than your average Australian airport at the event. He describes people screaming around him as the shots were heard. Cabinet ministers and other important people were being plucked from tables as the Secret Service started running through the room in "extraordinary" scenes.

items.title: Australian surgeon returns for 'very important' fourth mission in Gaza
items.description: Orthopaedic surgeon Herwig Drobetz returns to Gaza for fourth mercy mission.
